title: How Much Fiber in Kale? 4.7g per Cup
description: Kale: about 4.7 g of fiber per 1 cup, cooked (17% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in kale?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Kale, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

intro: Kale ranks #4 of 10 vegetables on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in kale by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in kale?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists kale, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt at 4 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup, cooked; 118 g) therefore has about 4.7 g of fiber and 42 calories. That is 17% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 19% of a 25 g day and 12% of a 38 g day.
Kale is a popular salad green, but like spinach, its fiber depends on whether it is raw or cooked. Cooked kale is a good source; a raw cup is light and adds less than a gram.

sections.heading: Massaged raw kale vs cooked
paragraphs: Massaging raw kale with a little oil and salt softens it and shrinks the volume, which lets you eat more kale in one bowl. Weigh it if you want a precise number, because cups of raw kale vary a lot with packing.
Kale chips concentrate the leaves. A bag can hold several cups of raw kale; check the label.

sections.heading: How kale compares with other vegetables
paragraphs: Of the 10 vegetables on this site, kale ranks #4 for fiber per typical serving and #2 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 11.1 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [spinach](/fiber-in-spinach) at 4.3 g (1 cup, cooked); [broccoli](/fiber-in-broccoli) at 5.1 g (1 cup chopped, cooked); [Brussels sprouts](/fiber-in-brussels-sprouts) at 4.1 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), kale is #5 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding kale to your day
paragraphs: Sauté a bunch of kale with garlic as a side, or stir it into bean soups. Two cups of raw kale become about half a cup cooked.

Example: 1 cup cooked kale, 1/2 cup chickpeas, 1 cup quinoa. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 16.1 g of fiber, with 4.7 g from the kale. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of kale?
faqs.a: 4 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Kale, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in kale (1 cup, raw (loosely packed))?
faqs.a: About 0.9 g (Kale, raw), for 21 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.
No. Cooking shrinks the leaves, so a cooked cup holds more kale and more fiber than a raw cup.

faqs.q: Is kale higher in fiber than lettuce?
faqs.a: Yes. Per 100 g, raw kale has roughly twice the fiber of romaine lettuce.
